body:
### Description

I'm working with a computational model in Python that involves multiple FFT/iFFT operations using CuPy 11.6.0 with the cuFFT backend. The model performed well with input arrays of size up to 2^27 elements (double complex), taking about 6.5 minutes to run. However, after increasing the array size to 2^28 elements, the runtime has drastically increased to approximately 10 hours.

My setup includes an i9 9900k CPU, 128 GB RAM, ASUS 4090 OC 24 GB GPU, running on Windows 10 (64-bit) with Python 3.7.7, CUDA Toolkit 12.3, NVIDIA driver 536.99.

Profiling with Nsight Compute has indicated warnings about kernels being launched with only 1 block and 1 grid. Unfortunately, I haven't found a way to adjust the cuFFT kernel configurations through CuPy. Attempts to use cupyx.optimizing.optimize were fruitless and, further, it cannot access cuFFT kernels.

I have a Nsight Compute report available:

https://drive.google.com/file/d/19mqFSwBZ3ghPMGrXqAcKlsdguH7AjuCU/view?usp=sharing (link to the compressed file, ~64 MB).

Please note that the file is large when uncompressed (~1GB) and may take some time to load in Nsight Compute 2023.3.0. This report is for the input array with 2^27 elements as Nsight Compute crashes with 2^28 elements.

The input data and python file to test the code can be retrieved here: 
Input data with 2^22 elements: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jG9Uqus8U5QJi7TzDUxCmnEiT80IoWbU/view?usp=sharing

Input data with 2^27 elements: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BT0ayq7gkJWKDTt3slX13HON1dxOfrBN/view?usp=sharing

Input data with 2^28 elements: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BT0ayq7gkJWKDTt3slX13HON1dxOfrBN/view?usp=sharing

Python code (to load the data (same as the above), pls just uncomment one of the lines 22/23/24): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1XmVqYMWU9ZuyaFk9kMCj1kr4YQo59AsT/view?usp=sharing

I'm seeking suggestions on how to address this issue, particularly with optimizing cuFFT kernel launches or managing large arrays in CuPy. Any insights or advice would be greatly appreciated. Thank you!

### To Reproduce

```py
import os
import time
from datetime import datetime
import cupy as cp
import cupyx.scipy.fft as cufft
import scipy.fft
scipy.fft.set_global_backend(cufft)


import joblib
from joblib import load

import cupyx.scipy.signal as cpx


def core():

# Get the directory of the current script
    script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

    # Construct the path to the file - Pls uncomment as needed! 
    joblib_file_path = os.path.join(script_dir, 'input_222.joblib') # array w/ 2^22 elements	
    #joblib_file_path = os.path.join(script_dir, 'input_227.joblib') # array w/ 2^27 elements
    #joblib_file_path = os.path.join(script_dir, 'input_228.joblib') # array w/ 2^28 elements

    # Load the input array
    data = joblib.load(joblib_file_path)

    L, gp, field, Dop, mnpc = data


    # Transfer data from CPU to GPU
    L = cp.asarray(L)

    gp = cp.asarray(gp)

    field = cp.asarray(field)

    Dop = cp.asarray(Dop)

    mnpc = cp.asarray(mnpc)

    # Setting loop initial conditions
    z = 0.0  #  position
    n = 0  # iteration counter

    # Shift the Dop operator 
    Dop_s = cufft.ifftshift(Dop)

    # Start loop for calculation
    start_loop = time.time()
    print(f" [{datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d at %H:%M:%S')}] Loop has started ... ")

    while z < L:

        gE2 = gp * cp.abs(field) ** 2
        id_max = cp.argmax(gE2)
        h = min(mnpc / gE2[id_max], L - z)

        # Calculate Dop for reuse
        exp_Dop_h= cp.exp(Dop_s * h / 2.0)

        # First operators action (frequency and time domain)
        field = cufft.ifft(cufft.fft(field, overwrite_x=True) * exp_Dop_h, overwrite_x=True)
        field *= cp.exp(-1j * gp * cp.abs(field) ** 2 * h)

        # Second operator action (frequency domain)
        field = cufft.ifft(cufft.fft(field, overwrite_x=True) * exp_Dop_h, overwrite_x=True)

        z += h
        n += 1

        #print(f'h = {h}, n = {n}, and z = {z}')
        
    end_loop = time.time()
    
    print(f" [{datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d at %H:%M:%S')}] Loop finished after {(end_loop - start_loop):.2f} seconds and {n} steps \n")

    field = cp.asnumpy(field)	

    return field


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Capture the start time
    start_time = time.time()
    print(f"\n [{datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d at %H:%M:%S')}] Job started\n")

    # Call the Solver function
    result = core()

    # Capture the end time
    end_time = time.time()
    print(f" [{datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d at %H:%M:%S')}] Job finished ")

    # Calculate and print the total job time
    total_time = end_time - start_time
    print(f" Total job time: {total_time:.2f} seconds")
```
